messages:
oncall-bot: INCIDENT ALERT — multiple 500s observed from serving-runtime in eu-west2. Error aggregated: CUDA illegal memory access (misaligned address). Paging spikes correlated. Link: https://incidents.redwood/2065004321
oncall-bot: Severity: P1. Auto-page to #incidents and p1-oncall.
Maya Ramos: seeing repeated container restarts on node gpu-eu-12, logs show 'CUDA_ERROR_ILLEGAL_ADDRESS' and 'misaligned address during device memcpy'. Started around 10:42 UTC, traffic spike from a large customer run.
Ethan Li: can you paste the dmesg / kernel oops? node id & container image?
Maya Ramos: node=gpu-eu-12, pod=redwood-runtime-v2-7f8c9, image=redwood/runtime:v2.3.1+opt. dmesg excerpt:
```
[ 12345.678901] NVRM: Xid (PCI:0000:65:00): 79, pid=21543, cid=0(ffff800012345678) 0x00000000
[ 12345.678912] cuda0: illegal memory access at 0x7fffa0000ef0
[ 12345.678920] gpu-worker[21543]: kernel: misaligned address in memcpy_async
```
Maya Ramos: also saw rapid page-ins (~1.8GB/s) and OOM killer traces around same time.
Priya Singh: probable interaction between our continuous-batching kernel and the recent kernel backport on that node image. Has this node got the new nvidia-driver/kernel combo?
Carlos Torres: confirmed gpu-eu-12 was provisioned with driver 525.85 and kernel 6.1.11-bp (backported). Other nodes still on 525.60 + 5.15.
eng-runtime: we've seen a regression in async memcpy paths on 525.85 with certain alignment patterns. Suspect race with KV cache evictions touching stale pointers.
Ethan Li: mitigation options: 1) cordon + drain node to stop further crashes; 2) scale down current model replicas on that node; 3) roll runtime back to v2.3.0 which uses safe memcpy paths; 4) enable fallback to CPU for affected model shards (performance impact).
ops-lead: doing (1) cordon gpu-eu-12 now. ETA for drain ~2m.
ops-lead: drain started — evicting 4 pods. Some pods failed termination due to GPU driver OOM; forcing delete 2. Noting potential customer impact.
Maya Ramos: applying runtime flag --batching.max_tokens=256 for the model-route to reduce large contiguous mem copies (temp). Pushing config change.
eng-runtime: patch ready to redirect memcpy to checked-path on runtime; can hotpatch one pod at a time. But if kernel driver bug triggers, best to restore to driver 525.60 nodes.
Carlos Torres: initiating rollback of node image pool to driver 525.60 in eu-west2 pool for all new auto-replacements. Current nodes will be cordoned.
customer-success-bot: Alerting affected customers: IDs 8721, 9912 had increased 500s during 10:42-10:55 UTC. CS pinged; prep status update.
Priya Singh: routing policy: failover to fallback model-variant `gpt-small-fallback` in other region for high-priority customers. Initiating rollout now.
Ethan Li: manual pod restart on one hotpatch candidate succeeded (no illegal memory on restarted pod, logs show 'memcpy_safe path used'). But another restarted pod still hit the error within 30s. Racey.
eng-runtime: starting full trace collection on one affected node (KGPU trace + ptrace) — this will be noisy. Need to keep one node alive for repro.
ops-lead: mitigation summary: cordoned gpu-eu-12, drained 3/4 pods (1 forced delete), reduced batch size for route, hotpatch attempted on rolling pod (mixed success), started image rollback for new replacements, initiated cross-region failover for priority customers.
Maya Ramos: customer impact: intermittent 503/500 for ~10% of requests to the heavy-batch endpoint between 10:42-10:56 UTC. No data leak. Latency spikes for others while failover in progress.
customer-success-bot: Status note drafted and sent for customers 8721/9912. Ops notified legal & security.
eng-runtime: root cause hypothesis: driver 525.85 introduced an alignment-unsafe path in async memcpy that races with our KV cache shard eviction. When the cache eviction frees a host-mapped buffer concurrently with device memcpy, misaligned device pointer deref occurs -> illegal access.
Priya Singh: next actions: replicate on repro node with a synthetic workload (high C x batch, long seq), coordinate with NV driver team, prepare rollback plan for all eu-west2 nodes if repro confirmed, postmortem scheduled.
Maya Ramos: creating incident board and timeline. tagging postmortem owners: Priya & Ethan.
ops-lead: lowering severity to P2 for now since failover completed for high-priority customers and crash rate reduced. We'll keep the page open until postmortem complete.
eng-runtime: collect and upload GPU core dumps + full dmesg to secure bucket: s3://redwood-incident-dumps/2065004321/
Maya Ramos: thanks all — will update once NV team responds or repro finishes. :thumbsup:
